title: The Power of Compound Interest
summary: How compound interest grows wealth over time — and why starting early matters.

scenes.title: The Magic of Compound Interest
scenes.narration: Compound interest is when your earnings start earning money too, creating a powerful snowball effect. It's often called 'interest on interest' and can turn small savings into substantial wealth over time.

scenes.title: Simple vs. Compound: The Key Difference
scenes.narration: Unlike simple interest, which only calculates returns on the initial principal, compound interest adds earned interest back to the principal. This means your investment base continuously grows, accelerating wealth accumulation.

scenes.title: The Compounding Formula
scenes.narration: The formula A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) shows how principal (P), rate (r), time (t), and compounding frequency (n) determine the final amount (A). The more frequent the compounding, the faster your money grows.

scenes.title: Real-World Impact: Retirement Savings
scenes.narration: A common application is retirement savings, where early investments benefit significantly from compounding. For example, $10,000 invested at 7% annual interest for 30 years could grow to over $76,000, illustrating the power of time.

scenes.title: The Eighth Wonder of the World
scenes.narration: Albert Einstein famously called compound interest the 'eighth wonder of the world' due to its ability to generate significant wealth over long periods. Understanding this principle is crucial for making informed financial decisions and achieving financial goals.
